description: PostgreSQL MCP Server Configuration via MCP Toolbox for Databases (the archived @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres is deprecated)

available_tools._comment: Tool names come from the Toolbox prebuilt Postgres tool set and vary by version; run /mcp in a session to list what the connected server actually exposes.

execute_sql.description: Execute a SQL statement against the database
example_prompts: Query the users table for accounts created in the last week
Get the count of tickets grouped by category
Describe the schema of the tickets table

list_tables.description: List all tables in the database
example_prompts: List all tables in the database

variables.POSTGRES_USER: Role to connect as; use a read-only role
variables.POSTGRES_PASSWORD: Set in your shell, never in the file

use_read_only_user.description: Create a dedicated read-only user for Claude Code
sql: GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE mydb TO claude_reader;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO claude_reader;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO claude_reader;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO claude_reader;
REVOKE SELECT ON sensitive_table FROM claude_reader;

use_connection_pooling.description: Use PgBouncer or similar for production

example_queries.basic_select: SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE status = 'open' LIMIT 10;
example_queries.aggregation: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM tickets GROUP BY category;
example_queries.join: SELECT t.id, t.content, u.email FROM tickets t JOIN users u ON t.user_id = u.id;
example_queries.date_filter: SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days';

permissions_example._comment: MCP tool permissions use the form mcp__<server>__<tool>. Permission rules match whole tools, not SQL verbs inside an argument, and Toolbox exposes SQL through a single execute_sql tool, so read-only enforcement belongs in the database grant (see security_recommendations above) or in a PreToolUse hook that inspects the query text.
